description: Join Gradient Desperadossss! We are tackling the Moon/Mars Earth Analogs challenge by writing a purely academic Systematic Literature Review (SLR) and research proposal without any coding. We are actively looking for technical writers, researchers, and space science enthusiasts to help us build a solid publication framework.
summary: Gradient Desperadosss presents a preliminary systematic evidence synthesis and comparative framework for identifying terrestrial environments relevant to lunar South Pole exploration and future Mars missions. Our research evaluates five established Earth analog sites alongside two Pakistani candidates, Hingol/Makran and Katpana Cold Desert. Using NASA imagery, planetary science literature, and a PRISMA-informed methodology, we developed five comparative matrices to assess geological, environmental, and operational similarities, limitations, and future testing opportunities. The project provides a transparent research framework rather than a completed systematic review or validated planetary site-ranking system.
details:
Project Overview

Gradient Desperadosss presents From Earth to the Moon and Mars, a preliminary systematic evidence synthesis and comparative analytical framework developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

Our project addresses the challenge of identifying terrestrial environments that could support future lunar South Pole exploration and Martian surface missions.

What Does Our Project Do?

Rather than developing a traditional software application, our team created a research-based framework to compare Earth environments with specific geological, environmental, and operational requirements of the Moon and Mars.

We examined five established terrestrial analog locations: the Atacama Desert, Haughton Crater, Death Valley, McMurdo Dry Valleys, and Mauna Kea. We also investigated two Pakistani candidates, Hingol/Makran in Balochistan and Katpana Cold Desert in Skardu.

How Does It Work?

Our approach uses a PRISMA-informed literature review protocol, NASA-related imagery, verified scholarly references, and comparative evidence matrices.

We assembled a research library of 40 authenticated publications, including eight provisionally selected primary studies. Relevant sections of 26 curated reports were examined.

Five comparative matrices evaluate geological characteristics, terrain morphology, environmental conditions, surface materials, evidence confidence, and possible mission-testing applications.

Our framework distinguishes scientifically observed properties from proposed planetary applications and explicitly identifies where similarities break down.

NASA Data and Research Tools

The project uses NASA Worldview imagery for terrestrial context, lunar visualizations attributed to the NASA Planetary Data System Orbital Data Explorer, and a documented HiRISE image of Mars.

Additional resources include scientific publications, Crossref, OpenAlex, Europe PMC, USGS documentation, and PRISMA 2020 guidance.

We used OpenAI Codex and ChatGPT to assist with literature organization, preliminary evidence synthesis, scientific writing, reference checking, comparative tables, and document preparation. LaTeX and Overleaf were used to produce the final research manuscript.

No application, machine-learning model, custom software system, hardware prototype, field experiment, or new quantitative planetary raster analysis was developed.

Creativity and Innovation

Our research emphasizes task-specific planetary analog selection rather than visual resemblance alone.

An important regional contribution is the comparative evaluation of Hingol/Makran and Katpana as potential future research environments. These locations are proposed candidates, not experimentally validated planetary analogs.

We also developed an evidence-to-test framework connecting observed terrestrial characteristics with potential planetary research questions and future validation requirements.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The framework can help researchers identify suitable environments for studying planetary geology, sediment processes, robotic mobility, scientific instruments, regolith handling, and exploration procedures.

It also highlights research opportunities in Pakistan and provides a structured foundation for future field characterization and laboratory testing.

Research Limitations

This project is a preliminary systematic evidence synthesis, not a completed systematic literature review. Comprehensive searching, final eligibility assessment, independent scientific appraisal, and some imagery provenance verification remain incomplete.

These limitations are explicitly documented in our research paper. Further scientific validation is required before the proposed candidate locations can be considered established planetary testing environments.

Deliverable: IEEE-style research manuscript with five comparative matrices, six figures, scientific references, and a proposed planetary analog evaluation framework.
dataRefs: NASA Worldview - Terrestrial imagery supplied for the Atacama Desert regional comparison. Exact original export metadata remains provisional.

NASA Planetary Data System Orbital Data Explorer - Lunar reference imagery and documentation relating to LRO LOLA topography, LROC WAC mosaics, and the Lunar Orbiter Global Digital Mosaic. Exact layers used in the supplied image exports remain unverified.
HiRISE - Mars image PSP_007925_1990, used as a documented visual reference for the Jezero crater delta environment.
